caption.scope: Simplified architecture of the T1D simulator, showing the three player-controlled input pathways (food, insulin, activity) and how they connect to the Hovorka 2004 glucose-insulin core and simulator-specific extensions. Plasma insulin I acts on glucose pools Q1/Q2 via three effect compartments (x1: transport, x2: peripheral disposal, x3: EGP suppression). Stress hormones and exercise modulate hepatic glucose production and peripheral disposal, respectively. Ketogenesis is determined by plasma insulin level. The CGM sensor reads interstitial glucose with a diffusion delay. Compartments gut (D1, D2) and sc (S1/S2 + S1b/S2b) each roll up two ODE states into a single block — this is a deliberate overview-level simplification; each subsystem is detailed in its own sub-model figure.

variables.definition: carbohydrate / fat / protein content of a meal (player input)
rapid (bolus) and basal insulin doses (player input, mU)
heart rate and exercise type driving the exercise dynamics (player input)
gut absorption cascade: stomach (D1) and intestine (D2) compartments — see gut sub-model figure
subcutaneous insulin depots: two-stage rapid cascade (S1, S2) and parallel basal shadow cascade (S1b, S2b) — see insulin PK sub-model figure
exercise effect compartments: fast GLUT4-mediated uptake (E1) and slow post-exercise insulin sensitivity (E2)
stress hormone state: acute catecholamine surge and chronic hypercortisol contribution to EGP elevation
plasma insulin concentration (mU/L)
insulin effect compartments: x1 = glucose transport (Q1 to Q2), x2 = peripheral disposal, x3 = EGP suppression
endogenous (hepatic) glucose production = EGP0 * max(0, stress - x3)
glucose pools: Q1 = plasma glucose (BG = Q1 / V_G), Q2 = peripheral (intracellular) glucose
beta-hydroxybutyrate — dominant ketone body; rate of production gated by plasma insulin level
interstitial glucose concentration read by the CGM sensor (mmol/L)
glucose appearance rate from gut into plasma (mmol/min)
rapid insulin appearance rate from SC depot into plasma (mU/min)
basal insulin appearance rate from SC shadow cascade into plasma (mU/min)
build-up rate constant driving I into effect compartments (kb1, kb2, kb3 for x1, x2, x3)
insulin-independent glucose uptake (brain, red blood cells, etc.) — fixed ~0.0097 * weight mmol/min
renal glucose excretion: occurs when plasma glucose exceeds ~9 mmol/L (renal threshold)
interstitial diffusion rate constant (~0.073 /min, giving ~14 min CGM lag)
